In semantics , mathematical logic and related disciplines, the principle of compositionality (also known as semantic compositionalism ) is the principle that the meaning of a complex expression is determined by the meanings of its constituent expressions and the rules used to combine them. The principle is also called Frege's principle , because Gottlob Frege is widely credited for the first modern formulation of it. However, the principle has never been explicitly stated by Frege, [ 1 ] and arguably it was already assumed by George Boole decades before Frege's work. [ 2 ]
